chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn 'Uthafir, from Umar ibn Yazid, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

The resident of Mecca performs the 'Umrat al-Tamattu' (pilgrimage with a single body for 'Umrah and Hajj) for two years; if he exceeds two years, he becomes a Qari' (one who performs Hajj al-Qiran or Hajj al-Mufrad depending on context, here implying a different status where Tamattu' is no longer valid) and it is not permissible for him to perform 'Umrat al-Tamattu'.

key_terms.بِالْعُمْرَةِ إِلَى الْحَجِّ: With 'Umrah until Hajj (referring to the combination of the two rituals)
key_terms.وَلَيْسَ لَهُ: And it is not for him/permissible for him
key_terms.يَتَمَتَّعُ: He performs Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where one performs 'Umrah first, then releases from Ihram, and re-enters for Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a resident of Mecca performing Umrah and Hajj together?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a two-year threshold for determining whether a resident of Mecca is considered a 'muqim' (resident) or 'mu'tadir' (visitor), thereby governing their eligibility for 'Umrat al-Tamattu'. This ruling highlights the jurisprudential distinction between permanent residents and temporary visitors, ensuring that the ritual of combining 'Umrah and Hajj remains accessible to those who do not have a fixed domicile in the holy city.
